question: A 13-year-old girl asks for an HIV self-test kit at OPD without a parent. Can she consent on her own?
label: reason_first

blocks.text: No. She cannot consent on her own because she is only 13 years old and HIVST requires a verbal consent for individuals 12 years and above.
However, if she were considered an emancipated minor or mature adult, she could provide informed consent for treatment, including HIV testing.

references: [2] Amendment to the Eswatini Integrated HIV Management Guidelines (2024), Assisted and Unassisted – WHO Definition, PDF page 9
[3] hiv-2022, Health Care Consent and Assent for Children and Adolescents, PDF page 228
message:
No. She cannot consent on her own because she is only 13 years old and HIVST requires a verbal consent for individuals 12 years and above.

However, if she were considered an emancipated minor or mature adult, she could provide informed consent for treatment, including HIV testing.

Sources: [2] Amendment to the Eswatini Integrated HIV Management Guidelines (2024), Assisted and Unassisted – WHO Definition, PDF page 9; [3] hiv-2022, Health Care Consent and Assent for Children and Adolescents, PDF page 228

However, if she were considered an emancipated minor or mature adult, she could provide informed consent for treatment, including HIV testing.

key_facts: [2] The age of consent for HIVST has been reduced from 16 years to 12 years.
Children under 12 years can provide informed consent for treatment if they are considered an emancipated minor or mature adult.

[3] Anyone 12 years or older can give informed consent for medical care such as HIV testing services (HTS), PrEP, PEP, family planning, or medical male circumcision according to the 2012 Swaziland Child Welfare Act, but not for HIV treatment.

question: Adult outpatient newly diagnosed with HIV, CD4 is 180. Should I send serum CrAg and urine TB-LAM?
label: reason_first

blocks.text: Yes. Start serum CrAg screening now: adults living with HIV, start if CD4 ≤200 cells/ml regardless of TB signs and symptoms, inpatients and outpatients.

No. Do not start urine TB-LAM yet: symptomatic patients: all patients regardless of CD4 count with TB signs and symptoms; seriously ill patients*: all patients regardless of CD4 count or TB signs and symptoms; inpatients and outpatients: CD4 ≤200 cells/ml regardless of TB signs and symptoms.

references: [1] hiv-amendment-2024, Advanced HIV package, PDF page 25

[4] hiv-2022, Advanced HIV package of care (continued), PDF page 133

question: Child living with HIV, 5 kg, starting first-line ART. Can I use the pALD (ABC/3TC/DTG 60/30/5 mg) dispersible tablet?
label: reason_first

blocks.text: No, you cannot use the pALD (ABC/3TC/DTG 60/30/5 mg) dispersible tablet.
The child weighs 5 kg, which is below the minimum weight of 6 kg for using the new FDC pALD.

references: [1] Amendment to the Eswatini Integrated HIV Management Guidelines (2024), Paediatric pALD (ABC-3TC-DTG) dispersible tablet (DT), PDF page 36
[2] hiv-amendment-2024, Paediatric ARV dosing chart including pALD, PDF page 37
